events.summary: STRL rose 5.6% to $533.42 on Friday. No company news, filing or analyst action was found for the day. The whole market rallied after a weak September jobs report: the US added only 29,000 jobs and unemployment rose to 4.2%, both weaker than expected; traders cut the odds of an October Fed rate hike to 21% from 64% the week before. S&P 500 +0.73%, Nasdaq +1.19% (record), Dow +0.49%; industrials were among the leading sectors.
events.why_it_matters: The pipeline attribution says 2.25 points of the 5.6% came from the market and 1.96 points from the industry (PAVE), leaving only +1.39 points company-specific (z-score 0.31, i.e. a normal day for this stock). STRL has a 1-year beta of about 3 vs the market, so it amplifies market moves both ways. This is not new information about Sterling's business.

events.summary: Sterling bought substantially all assets of Stone Ridge Contracting (Pocatello, Idaho; heavy civil, concrete and construction management for data centers, mining and industrial sites in ID, OR, ND, WA, TX). Closed 2026-06-01 for $178.0 million total: $140.0 million cash and about 32 thousand shares worth $27.4 million, plus up to $15 million earn-out on an EBITDA target. Company expected Stone Ridge 2026 revenue of $180-200 million at mid-teens EBITDA margins.
events.why_it_matters: It adds data-center site work, but at mid-teens margins versus Sterling's ~22% company adjusted EBITDA margin, so it dilutes the margin percentage. This became the core of the post-earnings worry in August. Stone Ridge also brought $1.24 billion of unsigned awards into 'combined backlog'.

events.summary: Q2 2026: revenue $1.168B (+90%, about 50% organic), adjusted EPS $5.80 (+116%), GAAP EPS $5.00, adjusted EBITDA $256.7M (22% margin). Signed backlog $4.33B (+116%), combined backlog $5.62B, future phases >$1.4B. Beat consensus (revenue est. ~$963M, adjusted EPS est. ~$4.99-5.01). Full-year 2026 guidance raised to revenue $4.00-4.15B, adjusted EPS $19.70-20.30, adjusted EBITDA $891-916M (from $3.70-3.80B, $18.40-19.05, $843-873M given 2026-05-04). Yet the stock fell 13.39% after hours to $529.61 from a $611.47 close.
events.why_it_matters: A strong beat and raise still sent the stock down. The main explanation in coverage: the raise came mostly from lower-margin acquired revenue (incremental guidance margin about 14% vs ~22% today), and the price was already high (P/E ~47.6 at the time). Lesson: price depends on expectations and valuation, not just growth.

Cause of the market rally: a weak September jobs report (+29,000 jobs, unemployment 4.2%) cut the odds of an October Fed rate hike to 21% from 64% a week earlier.

Why that lifts STRL more than the market: lower expected interest rates help expensive growth stocks (future profits are worth more today) and ease worries about financing for big construction projects; STRL's 1-year beta is about 3, so it typically moves about three times the market.

products.name: E-Infrastructure Solutions (site development and electrical work for data centers and other mission-critical sites)
products.what_it_is: Getting a large plot of land ready for a data center, factory or warehouse: clearing, grading, excavation, foundations, underground utilities, and since the CEC deal (closed 2025-09-01) electrical contracting too.
products.analogy: Before a house can be built someone has to level the lot, dig the foundation and lay the pipes and wires; Sterling does that for buildings the size of several football fields.
products.buyers: Data-center developers and hyperscalers' contractors, plus manufacturing, semiconductor and e-commerce distribution builders. Customer names and concentration not disclosed in the Q2 10-Q.
products.how_it_works: Project contracts; revenue is recognized as work progresses. Signed contracts sit in 'backlog'; awarded-but-unsigned work sits in 'combined backlog'; expected later phases of the same campuses are 'future phases'.
products.sales: Q2 2026 segment revenue $905.0M (+192% YoY), 78% of company revenue; adjusted operating margin 24.1%. Mission-critical projects (data centers, manufacturing, semiconductor) were 92% of E-Infrastructure backlog at 2026-06-30. Company-wide signed backlog $4.33B, combined $5.62B, future phases >$1.4B (total visibility >$7B).
products.stage: Mature and scaling fast; capacity limited by skilled labor (CEO: more electricians would mean faster growth, per Q2 call coverage).
products.size_for_company: About 78% of Q2 2026 revenue and the large majority of operating income ($210.8M of segment operating income vs $28.2M Transportation and $8.5M Building).
products.competition: Not detailed in sources read; peers often grouped with it by investors include Quanta Services, Comfort Systems USA, EMCOR, MasTec, Dycom (all moved with STRL in the 2026-07-02 selloff).
products.why_investors_care: It is the growth engine and the reason the stock is treated as an 'AI data-center builder'. Its fate is tied to how long big tech keeps building data centers.
products.watch_next: Q3 2026 backlog, book-to-burn (Q2 was 1.4x signed ex Stone Ridge), E-Infrastructure margin after the Stone Ridge mix, any customer delays.
